opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
The commonality between these two readings is "how do we respond to God?"

In 2 Kings, King Zedekiah repeatedly hears God's message through Jeremiah but lacks the courage to obey. He fears people more than God, and his disobedience ends in the destruction of Jerusalem.

In the Gospel, the leper has no power or status. He simply comes to Jesus in faith: "Lord, if you will, you can make me clean." Jesus heals him and then tells him to obey the Law by showing himself to the priest and offering the gift prescribed by Moses. His faith leads to both healing and restoration.

The contrast is striking. A king who had everything refuses God's word and loses it all. A man who has nothing trusts Jesus and receives everything back.

The readings ask us one simple question: When God speaks, will we respond with fear like Zedekiah, or with trust like the leper? God's grace is always offered, but it bears fruit in hearts willing to believe and obey.
